releases.name: v1.27.7 — authority envelope, persona/profile contract, and Claude Code runner anchoring
releases.body:
- **Authority envelope (R1.1, R1.3, R1.4):** the execution gate denies work without an operational layer; a missing or invalid layer pauses with an actionable message and a deterministic `flowtask authority repair`; installation is transactional, defaults to `assistant` autonomy, and rolls back on failure.
- **Two-value autonomy and two-layer identity (R2):** `assistant` and `autonomous-dev` only, fail-closed; the retired development layer is gone from the versioned tree; runner parity exceptions are tracked by SHA-256.
- **Persona and profile contract (R3):** personas carry tone and pedagogy only; `profile.json` has a single six-field shape validated on write; an invalid persona warns without blocking; the Tester reads `policy.profile`.
- **Code hygiene contract:** a project-agnostic skill plus planner, constructor, and validator wiring for style, conventions, and dead-code rules.
- **Claude Code adapter:** the runner agent is anchored at session start, agent skills resolve from the active runtime payload, and Engram tool permissions are available as an explicit opt-in.
- **Installer and update:** per-user web search reconciliation, worktree-manager decoupling, framed update dashboard, and Windows/Python fixes.

releases.name: v1.27.0 — English documentation, agnostic model selector, and worktree manager distribution
releases.body:
FlowTask 1.27.0 consolidates the distribution, testing, and documentation work delivered since 1.26.0: the model selector becomes an agnostic package, the worktree manager ships as a managed global dependency and an npm package, testing becomes gap-driven, and all user-facing documentation and messages are now in English.

## Agent model selector
- Extracted `flowtask-model-selector` into the agnostic `agent-model-selector` repository (Bun workspaces: core + OpenCode adapter).
- Consumed as a submodule; the installer allowlist and legacy cleanup keep installs idempotent.

## Worktree manager
- Managed global installation with ownership and versioning; install and update leave the dependency operational.
- Standalone manager published on npm as `worktree-for-agents` (npm or pnpm, no bin, no npx), with its MCP guide in `initialize.instructions`.
- Worktree closures now produce readable, traceable squash commits with the work ID and a generic fallback.

## Testing and autonomy
- Gap-driven test policy: one test per real gap, ceiling of three; planner and plan-auditor governance updated.
- Persona, autonomy, and permissions layers consolidated in the operational flow.

## Documentation and language
- User-facing documentation, installer and CLI messages, the config README, the permission-gate plugin, and documentation filenames are now in English.
- Runtime message quotes and existing test assertions were aligned; no new tests.
- Removed the outdated README limits section.

Cumulative delivery since v1.26.0.

releases.name: v1.26.0 — Agent Loop: round-based control and operational autonomy
releases.body:
FlowTask 1.26.0 delivers the complete Agent Loop: durable control of every objective and the operational autonomy phase that replaces human waits with policies.

## Agent Loop control
- executions with their own identity: start, rounds, pause, resume, and closure with a verdict
- verifiable progress per round with citable evidence and a versioned baseline
- blocking invariants for scope, protected files, evidence, and workspace isolation
- deterministic termination with fixed precedence and reversible pause
- idempotency: retries and resumes without duplicating effects
- spend observability, with a soft warning and a hard stop only when the work declares it

## Operational autonomy
- policies replace routine waits; risk consents remain human
- live validation with closure and intermediate rounds and a three-state verdict
- layer identity per invocation, unique base names, and verification that stops on missing identity
- zero assumptions: source, state, and pause on unconfirmed material data
- requirements and plans with domain expertise and mediated communication between agents
- conditional test decision, with report generation and inheritance
- progressive context degradation with per-moment rules and verifiable recovery
- bounded parallel orchestration: verifiable independence, visible queue, separate traces, conflict containment, and degradation to sequential on any doubt

## Operation
- one CA per point, with its own validation and closure
- worktree closure with serialized integration and contained conflict
- installation regenerated to distribute the new skills

Cumulative delivery since v1.24.0.
